text:
ana: Heads up — burst of 504s noticed from dedicated GPU pods in eu-west-1 starting ~10:32 UTC. Errors look like model shard pulls failing, but only for some AZs. Suspect privatelink iface -> TGW routing + NAT hairpin.

mike: Can you paste the error snippet? is this during model warmup or steady state?

ana: Mostly warmup/first pulls after scale-up. Example from pod logs: `GET https://models-repo.internal.redwood/api/v1/models/x/weights -> 504`

jess: I checked the NAT GW metrics — short, repeated spikes in SNAT translations coincident with the time window. TGW attachments for the cluster subnets show traffic routed out to a NAT in a different account.

kai: That rings a bell — did we recently move the privatelink interface endpoint for models-repo into the TGW-attached subnet (so it can be shared across VPCs)? If so, Private DNS might be resolving to the interface endpoint private IP, but the traffic is being hairpinned out to NAT because of route/sg asymmetry.

ana: Yup, infra change yesterday: moved iface endpoint ENI into shared-services subnet behind TGW to centralize. I can repro a traceroute from a failing pod:

```
traceroute to models-repo.private (10.200.5.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12)  0.4 ms  0.3 ms  0.3 ms
 2  nat-gw-01 (10.0.1.1)  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
```

jess: That first hop should have been the ENI local path. Looks like RT table for the pod subnet points default to TGW and then NAT in central account. The interface endpoint ENI health checks fine but source IP is getting SNAT'd, so downstream sees public EIP and returns via NAT.

mike: Are the ENI security groups only allowing inbound from the originating VPC/CIDR? If the cluster CIDR isn't allowed then the connection might be failing and the client retries, hitting fallback to public EIP via NAT.

ana: ENI SG only allowed 10.0.0.0/16 and 10.1.0.0/16. Our GPU nodes are in 10.2.0.0/16 (new AZ) — we forgot to update the SG. Oops.

kai: That explains asymmetric path: DNS->private IP, but ENI rejects 10.2.x so client retries or falls back and hits public EIP via NAT causing SNAT churn and 504s. Quick fix: add 10.2/16 to iface SG and add a route on the TGW attachment to prefer local path to ENI. Also consider enabling endpoint policy to explicitly allow service traffic.

jess: Rolling that change now. Adding SG rule first to avoid dropping traffic. Also bumping NAT GW autoscaling (increase elastic IP pool) to handle current surge.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1123 — Privatelink hairpin -> 504s on gpu-pool-eu-west-1. Pager duty triggered.

ana: After SG open + route tweak, pods started succeeding within 2 minutes. Still seeing some cached failures from nodes that had DNS cached public EIP — plan to restart kube-proxy/DNS cache on affected nodes to flush.

mike: Followups: (1) add 10.2/16 to endpoint SG via automation, (2) enforce infra PR that any iface moved into shared subnets requires SG sync with consumer VPC CIDRs, (3) add alert for sudden SNAT rate increase on NAT GW, (4) document pitfall in privatelink+TGW design (DNS vs SG vs route asymmetry).

kai: I can add a preflight check in the migration runbook that verifies SG contains all consumer CIDRs and that TGW route table prefers local route for endpoint ENI.

jess: Punting long-term fix: consider consolidating model repo access under central privatelink with endpoint in each consumer VPC (avoid TGW hairpin), or enable endpoint network interface in every AZ with correct SGs. Need cost / capacity tradeoff analysis.

ana: Thanks all. Marking incident resolved after node DNS cache restarts and automation PR raised: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/4523 :thumbsup:

mike: Nice catch — adding to postmortem notes.
